newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira ERM rate should stick to market rates - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Lira ERM rate should stick to market rates - Dini.

text.p: The level at which the lira eventually returns to the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) should not diverge from market rates, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Monday.
"The lira has shown itself to have its own strength, its own basic stability, even after the recent interest rate change," Dini told reporters.

"This is therefore a market rate and it will be difficult for Italy or for other countries to consider a re-entry exchange rate that diverges from the market rate where the lira has stayed largely stable for months," he added.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was quoted as telling German daily Welt am Sonntag at the weekend that the government wanted to apply later this month to put the lira back into the ERM at "slightly above 1,000 per mark."
Dini said he totally agreed with Ciampi's position regarding the lira.
The lira has recently been trading in a range slightly above the 1,000 level to the German mark. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
